clue.text: Where things are fitted together, boss helps Amy getting sorted out (12, two words)

indicators.note: things being sorted out are put into a new order, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A workplace where the manager pitches in to help a worker called Amy get organised.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly shop is the part of a factory where components are put together into finished products.

clue.text: Sidewalks fringing legendary mount and woodland shrub

indicators.note: a fringe runs round the edge of something, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: paves taken as pavements, the pedestrian walkways beside a road
Arkle was a celebrated Irish steeplechaser of the 1960s

explanation.surface: Pavements bordering a statue of some famous horse, with some shrubbery nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: Arkle, the legendary racehorse, sits inside PAVES after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Park-leaves is a name for tutsan, a St John's wort shrub that grows in woods and hedgerows.

clue.text: Bit of butter on some bread cut for scout

indicators.note: something cut is trimmed short, so the bread word loses its final letter
in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so this piece is written first

blocks.note: a pat is a small shaped piece of butter
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A breakfast instruction to put a dab of butter on a bit of trimmed bread for a young scout.
explanation.definitionFit: To scout is to reconnoitre, and a patrol goes out to do exactly that, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Contrarily heading for exposure in pergolas? (8, two words)

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
in places one piece inside the word that follows it

blocks.note: arbours are leafy garden shelters much like pergolas
first letter of exposure

explanation.surface: Perversely aiming to sunbathe inside garden pergolas.
explanation.walkthrough: A rebours is a French phrase taken into English; the question mark flags pergolas as an example of the garden shelters meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebours means against the grain or the wrong way round, which is acting contrarily.

clue.text: Traveller from Indonesia going round ME sultanate

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so the first piece wraps the second

blocks.note: RI is the international vehicle code for the Republic of Indonesia
Oman is a sultanate in the Middle East, ME

explanation.surface: A voyager from Indonesia touring an Arabian sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: Romani people are the Roma, historically a travelling people, and the word also names a member of that group.

clue.text: Titled chap holding everything up, an idle fellow

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the word is turned backwards
holding something keeps it inside, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a lord is a man with a title
all means everything

explanation.surface: A nobleman supporting the whole lot, though he is a layabout.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records lollard as a variant of loller, an idler, alongside its sense of a follower of Wycliffe.

clue.text: Snake climbing, right inside tree

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue goes from bottom to top, so the word is read backwards
inside puts one piece within the other

blocks.note: a naga is a snake, especially a cobra in Indian myth
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A snake slithers up a tree, right into its branches.
explanation.definitionFit: The argan is a Moroccan tree whose kernels yield argan oil.

clue.text: Go left for The Falconers' Band

blocks.note: go in the sense of energy and dash
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave, as if heading off to see a band called The Falconers.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make The Falconers' Band look like a music group; it is a ring on a hawk's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A vervel is a small ring fixed to a hawk's leg, bearing the owner's name, used in falconry.

clue.text: Diet no longer, getting stuck into Easter venison

indicators.note: something stuck into a phrase is buried inside it, so the letters are found running within those words

blocks.note: the run of letters inside these two words

explanation.surface: Abandoning a diet to tuck into venison at Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: No longer marks an obsolete word: sterve is an old form of starve.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterve is an archaic spelling of starve, going without food, an extreme kind of dieting.

clue.text: Opposed to team bar? Careful thought formerly required

blocks.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a side is a team
rance is a Scots word for a bar or prop

explanation.surface: A query about whether one is against having a team bar, which needs some reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerance is an obsolete word for consideration, careful reflection on a matter.

clue.text: E.g a this, when played … does raga perhaps

definitions.text: E.g a this, when played … does raga perhaps

indicators.note: an instrument when played produces something new, so these combined letters are rearranged into the phrase that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the full set of letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician's note that this instrument, when played, performs a raga, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: this stands for the answer, and the answer plus E.G. A rearranges into DOES RAGA. Take EGA away from those letters and SAROD is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The sarod is a fretless lute of Indian classical music, the kind of instrument on which a raga is played.

clue.text: All ready (one assumes) for anti-mozzy stuff

indicators.note: the setter supplies no direction word, so solvers must assume the down entry is read upwards from the bottom

blocks.note: teed up, as a golf ball placed ready to strike

explanation.surface: Everything prepared, it seems, for repelling mosquitoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Mozzy is Australian and British slang for a mosquito.
explanation.definitionFit: DEET is the standard chemical insect repellent used against mosquitoes.

clue.text: Take against second half of spread

blocks.note: rec. abbreviates recipe, the Latin for take used on prescriptions
to in the sense of against, as in pressed ear to wall

explanation.surface: An instruction to oppose the latter part of some spread, perhaps of food.
explanation.walkthrough: Spread here is two facing pages of an open book, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: A recto is the right-hand page of an open book, so it forms the second half of a two-page spread.

clue.text: Timber support back to front in places of worship

indicators.note: back to front here means the rear letter is carried round to the front

blocks.note: temples are places of worship

explanation.surface: A wooden beam fitted the wrong way round in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemple is a crossbeam of timber used as a support or step in a mine shaft.

clue.text: Meagre encouragement – only a bit of it – making one sick-looking

indicators.note: only a bit of the phrase is used, so the letters lie within its words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Faint praise, even a little of it, leaves one feeling queasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Green describes the pale, nauseous complexion of someone about to be ill.

clue.text: Instruments for cutting clinging weed

blocks.note: first meaning: heavy butchers' choppers
second meaning: goosegrass, a sticky hedgerow plant

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a weed whose hooked bristles cling to clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchers' choppers are cleavers, and the plant goosegrass is also called cleavers because it cleaves, or sticks, to things.

clue.text: Nocturnal mammal ran amok in former meeting-place (7, two words)

indicators.note: running amok is wild and disordered movement, so the letters are scrambled
in puts the scrambled letters within the next word

blocks.note: a moot was an assembly or meeting place in Anglo-Saxon England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A night creature went berserk in an old assembly hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The moonrat is a Southeast Asian gymnure, a hedgehog relative that forages at night.

clue.text: I'm anything but grand – with hole in it the pantie needs mending

indicators.note: a hole in the middle of a word means its centre letter is missing
something that needs mending is broken, so its letters must be put back together differently

blocks.note: the with its middle letter gone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shabby pair of knickers with a hole in them needing repair.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand is a grand piano; the answer speaks as a small piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianette is a small upright piano, about as far from a concert grand as a piano gets.

clue.text: Macbeth's recurrent theme? His heart leads us into drama initially

indicators.note: his refers back to the Scottish king, and his heart is the central letter of that name
initially means the opening letter of each of the following words is taken

blocks.note: the central letter of the seven-letter name
first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A question about the theme that keeps returning in Shakespeare's Scottish play.
explanation.walkthrough: BLUID is Scots for blood, fitting the Scottish king's play, where blood recurs in image after image.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood is the recurring image of Macbeth, and bluid is the Scots spelling, apt for a Scottish tragedy.

clue.text: Recline where one often does? It's declared to be false

blocks.note: a bed is where one usually lies down
to lie is to recline

explanation.surface: A riddle about lying down, then a statement that something is untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals the insertion: where one often reclines is in bed, so the setter leaves the solver to put one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Belied means shown or represented as untrue, contradicted, close to being pronounced false.

clue.text: Bash maybe to flog tickets at inflated prices (7, two words)

blocks.note: the infinitive to signals the verb be
a tout resells tickets at a mark-up

explanation.surface: A party, perhaps, where someone sells overpriced tickets.
explanation.walkthrough: A tout is a British word for a ticket scalper; to do the job is to be a tout. Bash is a verb here, not a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To bash something out is to hammer it out, and beat out is the same, so bash is an example of beating out.

clue.text: Youngster devouring red bananas stuffed with bacon?

devouring takes something inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy wolfing down red bananas filled with bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Larding meat means threading it with strips of bacon fat, so larded meat is stuffed with bacon.

clue.text: Noun phrase: shortened form of it occurs in a peculiar talk

indicators.note: a shortened form loses part of the word, here its first letter, as in poetic contraction
occurs in means appears within the next phrase

blocks.note: taken as written
cant is the jargon peculiar to a group
it shortened to 't, as in 'twas

explanation.surface: A grammar note about where an abbreviation turns up in odd speech.
explanation.definitionFit: In linguistics an actant is a noun phrase that takes part in the action expressed by a verb.

clue.text: Repugnance I displayed in endless deference

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: duty is respect owed, deference
the ego is the I, the self

explanation.walkthrough: DÉGOÛT is a French word for disgust used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Degout is distaste or disgust, a near synonym of repugnance.

clue.text: Green mineral: it's taken from mine to level

indicators.note: taken from removes the word it from the following word

rase is a variant of raze, to level to the ground

explanation.surface: A miner's note that a green stone is dug out to level ground.

clue.text: Fortified retreat, separate, to leave when Queen's gone

to quit is to leave

clue.text: Geological formation is scorching – I kept inside

taken as written

clue.text: Cocktail ingredient man gives me when this

the part of me it changes into

clue.text: We'll be roused with naker for reveille?

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Snow goose, like a whitecap?

clue.text: Food stuffed with strong flavour about to turn foul
